narrative.intro: National Government Services recorded $278M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. National Government Services secured 8 awards so far, with an average award size of $34.8M and obligations up 6.6% year over year. Annual obligations have varied across the last six fiscal years: FY21 $256M, FY22 $254M, FY23 $285M, FY24 $186M, FY25 $261M, FY26 $278M. National Government Services wins are concentrated in three markets by NAICS: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers $204M, Computer Systems Design Services $64M, and Other Computer Related Services $10.3M. The current-year totals are partial because FY2026 is fiscal year to date. The figures are contract obligations except for award-value figures in the largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables when those appear as total contract values. This profile shows sustained activity in health insurance and IT services markets, with consistent multi-hundred-million-dollar annual obligations and a year-over-year increase entering FY2026.

sections.heading: What is driving National Government Services obligations in FY2026?
sections.body: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers is the largest market for National Government Services with $204M in obligations. Computer Systems Design Services and Other Computer Related Services add $64M and $10.3M respectively, reflecting IT and insurance-related work. The mix of large health insurance obligations and IT services explains the company’s total of $278M in FY2026 to date and the reported average award size of $34.8M.

sections.heading: How have National Government Services obligations changed over time?
sections.body: Obligations for National Government Services have fluctuated across the last six fiscal years, ranging from $186M in FY24 to $285M in FY23. The FY2026 to date total of $278M represents an increase, obligations up 6.6% year over year. The company’s record shows recurring multi-hundred-million-dollar annual obligations.
